- Model consistently underestimates peak prices, especially after sharp spikes (e.g., 48.12, 49.30, 51.55) — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such events.
- Overestimates early in the 30-day window, then underestimates later — apply a “mean reversion” correction: if forecast is > true for first 5–7 days, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Shows lag in reacting to true price spikes — forecast often peaks 1–3 days after actual spike; add 1–2 days of lagged true value as a buffer in next forecast.
- Underestimates low-price periods (e.g., 33.75, 35.14) — increase forecast by 1–3% for such periods to avoid “dip” underestimation.
- Overestimates mid-range values (e.g., 38–42) — apply a “cap” rule: if forecast > 42, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overfitting to recent trends.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to smooth out volatility — introduce a “volatility multiplier” (e.g., +1.5% for high volatility days) to capture sudden swings.
